correctness.rationale: For finite G, the restriction of each diagonal subsemigroup to GxG is a subgroup containing the diagonal and thus the graph of one normal subgroup congruence. Each cross-section is empty or a subgroup of that normal subgroup, forced by multiplication with (e,e). All products between four relation blocks are checked, giving a unique converse form. Symmetry and transitivity characterize exactly two congruences per normal subgroup. Independent direct exhaustive relation closure checks for C1,C2,C3,C4,V4 and constructed-form checks for S3 gave VERIFY_OK; the arbitrary-group claims rest on the full proof, not the finite runs.

value.rationale: The central two-component Clifford semigroup example singled out in recent literature receives a complete structural relation census, including its inclusion order and exact coefficient. The subgroup-lattice denominator distinguishes groups of the same order and gives a sequence with chi tending to 0 while the idempotent semilattice remains the fixed two-element chain. This is a motivated missing Clifford case and a new constraint on possible coefficient bounds, not an arbitrary computation.
